| Construct | Kind | Purpose | Reach for it when |

| `MemoryFileSystem` | Class | An in-memory implementation of core Effect's `FileSystem` service: an isolated virtual POSIX volume — files, directories, symlinks, hard links, open descriptors, temporary resources, globbing, watching — behind the standard `FileSystem.FileSystem` key. | in-memory FileSystem test double, seed files, inject faults, inspect writes, sync and promises ports, case-insensitive volume |
| `MemoryFileSystemDirent` | Interface | A directory entry as `readdir(path, { withFileTypes: true })` answers it. Literal: a symbolic link is a symbolic link, never its target's kind. | readdir withFileTypes entry from the promises port |
| `MemoryFileSystemErrnoError` | TypeAlias | The error a synchronous `node:fs` call throws: an `Error` carrying `code`, `syscall` and — for a path-based syscall — `path`, with node's message format (`"ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/x'"`). Built by `MemoryFileSystem.errno`. | node-shaped thrown error, fail a port fault like node:fs |
| `MemoryFileSystemFaultHandler` | TypeAlias | A fault handler for one `FileSystem` method. It receives the real call arguments (path, mode, options…), so a fault can be path- or mode-specific. Returning a value replaces the call — typically `Effect.fail(PlatformError.systemError({...}))`, a `Stream`/`Sink` for the `stream`/`sink`/`watch` members, though a canned success is equally valid; returning `undefined` **declines**, delegating the call to the wrapped filesystem. The return type is the method's own, so an injected failure is constrained to the method's `PlatformError` channel — a bare `new Error` does not typecheck. This delegate-by-default posture is the whole difference from `FileSystem.layerNoop`, which denies unlisted methods. | |
| `MemoryFileSystemFaultMethod` | TypeAlias | The members of `FileSystem.FileSystem` that a fault handler can intercept: every function-valued method, the `Stream`/`Sink`-returning trio (`stream`, `sink`, `watch`) included. Only `MemoryFileSystem.failTimes` is narrower — a transient fault substitutes a failing `Effect`, so it slots into the `Effect`-returning methods alone. | |
| `MemoryFileSystemFaults` | TypeAlias | The fault registration map for `MemoryFileSystem.makeFaulty` and `MemoryFileSystem.layerFaulty`: per intercepted method, either a `MemoryFileSystemFaultHandler` or — on the `Effect`-returning methods — a `MemoryFileSystemTransientFault`. Methods absent from the map are never intercepted. | |
| `MemoryFileSystemFaultsFactory` | TypeAlias | The factory form of `MemoryFileSystemFaults`: called with the filesystem being wrapped, it returns the fault map. Accepted wherever a fault map is. | |
| `MemoryFileSystemHandle` | Interface | A synchronously built memory volume with every view over it: the `FileSystem` service, the inspection `MemoryFileSystemVolume`, a stable layer, the two read-only ports, and synchronous mutators — for Promise-style suites that never touch `Effect`. | one volume every view, assert after the run, sync setup mutators, fault the ports |
| `MemoryFileSystemOptions` | Interface | Options shared by every seeded constructor. | seed root, case-insensitive volume, inject faults at build |
| `MemoryFileSystemPortOptions` | Interface | Options for a synchronous port built over a volume. | configure faults on a sync or promises port |
| `MemoryFileSystemPortStats` | Interface | The stats a `MemoryFileSystemSyncFileSystem` `stat`/`lstat` answers — the `node:fs` `Stats` subset a port consumer reads. | stat result for an injected port, file directory symlink checks |
| `MemoryFileSystemPromisesFaults` | TypeAlias | Fault handlers for a `MemoryFileSystemPromisesFileSystem`: each may return a replacement promise, throw (an errno built with `MemoryFileSystem.errno`), or return `undefined` to delegate. A handler that throws synchronously makes the call REJECT, as a real `fs/promises` call does; it never throws at the call site. | fault an injected fs/promises port, reject one path |
| `MemoryFileSystemPromisesFileSystem` | Interface | The read-only `node:fs/promises` subset an injected async walker needs, as `MemoryFileSystem.promisesFileSystem` exposes it over a volume. | test double for injected fs/promises walker, readdir withFileTypes |
| `MemoryFileSystemReadFileEncoding` | TypeAlias | The encodings `MemoryFileSystemPromisesFileSystem.readFile` accepts: UTF-8, spelled either way, bare or as node's `{ encoding }` options object. | |
| `MemoryFileSystemSeed` | Interface | A volume seed: absolute POSIX paths mapped to seed entries. | |
| `MemoryFileSystemSeedDirectory` | Interface | A seed entry describing a directory — built with `MemoryFileSystem.directory`. The only way a seed can express an *empty* directory, and the way a directory receives an initial permission mode. | |
| `MemoryFileSystemSeedEntry` | TypeAlias | One value in a `MemoryFileSystemSeed`: plain file contents (`string \| Uint8Array`, unchanged from the original seed shape), or a tagged entry describing a file with a mode, a directory, or a symbolic link. | |
| `MemoryFileSystemSeedFile` | Interface | A seed entry describing a file, optionally carrying its initial permission mode — built with `MemoryFileSystem.file`. | |
| `MemoryFileSystemSeedSymlink` | Interface | A seed entry describing a symbolic link — built with `MemoryFileSystem.symlink`. | |
| `MemoryFileSystemSyncFaults` | TypeAlias | Fault handlers for a `MemoryFileSystemSyncFileSystem`: each receives the real call arguments and may throw (an errno built with `MemoryFileSystem.errno`), return a replacement, or return `undefined` to delegate to the volume. | fault an injected sync filesystem port, throw errno for one path |
| `MemoryFileSystemSyncFileSystem` | Interface | The six synchronous file operations a consumer-supplied filesystem port needs — `exists`, `readFile`, `readDirectory`, `isDirectory`, `stat`, `lstat` — as `MemoryFileSystem.syncFileSystem` exposes them over a volume. | |
| `MemoryFileSystemTransientFault` | Interface | A transient fault built with `MemoryFileSystem.failTimes`: usable anywhere a fault handler is, it fails a fixed number of calls with a given `PlatformError` and then delegates forever after. | |
| `MemoryFileSystemVolume` | Interface | Synchronous, read-only inspection of one memory volume — the write-path counterpart to seeding, for asserting on what a program actually wrote without routing every assertion through an `Effect` read. | |
| `MemoryFileSystemVolumeStat` | Interface | The answer of `MemoryFileSystemVolume.lstat`. | literal lstat of a volume entry, kind size mtime |
| `NodeSyncFileSystem` | Class | A read-only, synchronous `FileSystem` over `node:fs`. | from `@effected/memfs/node-sync` — read real disk under Effect.runSync, synchronous read-only node filesystem |
